about: Glasses from their makers' data sheets. The index at the reference temperature, relative to air at that temperature and one atmosphere, is the Sellmeier formula n^2 - 1 = sum B_i lambda^2 / (lambda^2 - C_i), lambda in um and C_i in um^2. Its change with temperature is TIE-19's model of the absolute index with the constants the sheet gives; SCHOTT's IRG sheets give D0, E0 and lambdaTk, the change's rate at 22 C, so the model is linear in temperature. The temperature range, -55 to +75 C, is the one SCHOTT's earlier (2013) IRG sheets tabulate the change over. cte is the mean expansion coefficient, 1/K, over the range given.
